type_legend.unsafe_inference: A specific inference the counselor/scoring logic must never make
type_legend.scoring_hint: A directional suggestion for how existing or future scoring logic should weight something — not a specific formula
type_legend.data_gap: A concrete, currently-missing schema/field this research identified
type_legend.interpretation: How a fact should be read/presented to be honest about what it does and doesn't establish

rules.statement: Do not treat activities.organization_scope free text as a confirmed founder-vs-joined fact — it is an unverified proxy, and founding is evidence for both leadership and entrepreneurship at once.
Titles ('captain', 'president', 'founder') are near-zero evidence alone, generalizing lib/scoring/dimensions/leadership.ts's existing title-discount pattern to every dimension a role touches.
hours_per_week × weeks_per_year is an unbounded self-reported estimate — treat as a coarse ordering signal, never display as a computed precise total-hours figure.

No field captures grade level at time of activity; deriving it from start_date + graduation_year is an unsafe inference across curricula with different grade/age mappings (US/UK/Turkey differ) unless that mapping is explicitly encoded, which it is not today.
A populated URL field (repo_url/live_url/output_url) proves an artifact exists and is checkable, not that it is good, used, or well-received.
Free-text outcome_summary impact claims ('reached thousands of users') are claims, not verified outcomes, regardless of evidence_status.
verification_rejected must never be treated the same as self_reported downstream — a failed verification attempt is a negative signal, not an absence of one.

Never imply who confirmed an evidence_added record — the shipped schema does not capture verifier identity/type; a proposed additive verifier_type field is described but not implemented by this research.
The six commitment-axis levels (exposure...creation) are not summable into one cross-profile score — reads must stay per-activity.
Never numerically compare/combine grades across different grading scales without an explicit normalization step; absent metadata, the comparison is unknown, not an average.
A course record with no grade is missing data, not a zero.
A student_interests row with no linked activity/project/research evidence must never by itself raise this dimension's score — it is a stated preference.

Protects existing correct behavior: lib/scoring/dimensions/leadership.ts's small capped title-bonus should not be increased in future edits — that would regress the mission's 'no leadership from title alone' requirement.
Founding status cannot be reliably recovered from organization_scope free text today — infer at confidence no higher than low until a structured role field exists.
Read independence_level as a genuine strength gate, not decorative text — 'shadowed' and 'designed and ran independently' are different tiers even with identical duration/hours.
output_type = 'none' is not automatically weaker than a row with output — independence and methodology matter at least as much as output presence.
A project with none of live_url/repo_url/users_reached/revenue_amount populated is a plan, not executed entrepreneurship, regardless of description language.
revenue_amount and users_reached corroborate that execution happened; they are not magnitudes to rank profiles by.
Never rank students by raw summed volunteering hours alone — hours concentrated in one cause_area is a stronger signal than the same total spread across unrelated one-off events.
Beneficiary/'people served' counts are self-reported estimates regardless of evidence_status; never present without that qualifier.
An award's strength depends on selectivity/scope and result-tier as independent facts — 'national award' with unspecified scope reads at medium, not high, confidence.
An awards row with no discoverable link to an originating activity is lower-context and should read one confidence tier below an equivalent linked award.
A career_goals row with no plausibly-connected activity/project/work experience/opportunity is a stated intention, not demonstrated exploration — its age must never imply progress.
Count distinct sustained explorations, not total career-exposure event attendance — several one-day events don't sum to one focused, sustained exploration.
ongoing=true with no end_date, no output, and no recent updated_at movement should be read as stale, not actively strong — no specific decay function computed by this research.
A complexity/impact claim in free-text description carries materially less weight than the same claim with a corroborating URL — description is a claim about evidence, not evidence.
Never model recognition as one flat list mixing result-tier, output-type, and role together (the mission brief's own example list does this) — keep the three (plus scope) as independent axes.
registered tier must never feed any ProfileDimension score above a negligible floor — it demonstrates intent, not development.

Core proposed fix: awards_distinction should only activate at advanced/qualified result tier or above; below that, credit only the category's participation-level dimensions. Directly closes the gap where entering and winning a competition produce identical CATEGORY_DIMENSIONS output today.
Do not assign a specific numeric scope multiplier in this research — scope is a qualitative modifier on result tier, never merged into one combined prestige score.
An award with scope=unknown should read one confidence tier below an otherwise-identical record with known scope.

A summer program that culminates in a publication should not have its own attendance credit inflated by the publication — model as two linked facts (program participation + research output), not one merged one.
Selectivity-at-entry (most fellowships) and selectivity-at-result (most competitions) are different mechanisms and must not share one gating rule.

rules.statement: Breadth dimensions (intellectual_curiosity, career_exploration — code-verified to skip diminishing-returns aggregation) and depth dimensions (the other 7) serve different developmental purposes; a counselor must be able to recommend a breadth/exploratory action without treating it as inherently lower-value than a depth action.

rules.source_section: §8 External validation and two structural principles (reconciliation pass)
rules.statement: Field/major alignment (already implemented as fieldAlignment/relevanceScore in lib/counselor/config.ts and lib/opportunities/matching.ts) is a relevance axis, not a development dimension — never conflate 'how strong is this evidence' with 'how well does it match stated interests.'

Derive an approximate developmental stage (yearsUntilGraduation = graduation_year - currentYear) from data ORYN already collects; expose it as a non-binding display default a student can override, never as a hard eligibility gate or a claim of precision it doesn't have. Degrade to 'insufficient data for timing context' for education_stage='other' or curriculum='other' rather than silently defaulting to one country's grade system.

Stage (years until graduation) determines WHAT KIND of recommendation is appropriate; the student's own time budget determines HOW MUCH/HOW BIG. Never let a tight time budget silently substitute a breadth-type recommendation for a depth-type one -- if nothing depth-appropriate fits, say so explicitly rather than swapping category.

A student outside the typical phase pattern for their stage is not automatically a gap. Distinguish objective time-remaining from implied deficiency: a Phase-1 student with genuine early depth should not be pushed toward artificial breadth; a Phase-2 student who is broad due to a recent, legitimate interest shift should have that context surfaced, not be penalized as if the shift never happened.

Treat 'Computer Science' as an umbrella, not a single skill -- competitive-programming-style algorithmic problem-solving and building/shipping user-facing products are both legitimately 'CS' but develop measurably different things.

When counseling a CS-interested student, distinguish at minimum three evidence types -- sustained independent build (execution_project_depth), algorithmic competition (quantitative/algorithmic reasoning under contest conditions), and time-boxed hackathon/team build (rapid-build + teamwork) -- rather than treating 'did something CS-related' as one undifferentiated signal.

'I like math' may mean enjoying proof/abstraction (pure track), applied problem-solving with formulas (applied track), or analyzing data (statistics track) -- these predict different downstream fits and should not be treated as one undifferentiated signal.

A stated interest in 'physics' or 'chemistry' should be probed for which pole a student actually enjoys -- theoretical/mathematical problem-solving vs. hands-on experimental work reward different exploration experiences.
'Biology' spans wet-lab/bench work, field/ecological work, and computational biology -- probing which a student means matters as much here as for computing/mathematics.

A biology major is necessary for essentially no clinical health profession in most systems -- pre-med 'requirements' are typically specific courses, not a mandated major. Must be stated explicitly to counteract a common real-world misconception.

'Engineering' as a stated interest is at least as broad as 'Computer Science' or 'Biology' -- a student should sample more than one of mechanical/civil/aerospace/electrical before narrowing, since they involve meaningfully different day-to-day work despite a shared first-year curriculum.

PE-equivalent licensure necessity varies substantially by role AND industry, not just by engineering subfield -- civil engineers stamping public infrastructure plans are the clearest necessity case; many ME/EE/AE industry roles (esp. aerospace/defense, tech-adjacent EE) practice career-long without one. A specific student's situation should be checked against target industry/employer expectations, not inferred from subfield alone.

Biomedical engineering is not a subset of 'pre-med' and should not be counseled as one -- it is an engineering discipline whose graduates mostly go into engineering/industry/research roles, not clinical practice. A student wanting to become a physician does not need a biomedical engineering degree. (Generalizes RULE-COUNSEL-208 to this field.)

Economics is a genuinely quantitative social science -- a student drawn to it purely for real-world relevance (news/policy) without appetite for the underlying statistics/econometrics is a real, worth-surfacing mismatch signal (a counseling conversation topic, not a disqualification).

Entrepreneurship is about originating and testing a new venture; general business/management study is about operating and improving an existing one. A strong management-track profile is not automatically evidence of entrepreneurial capability, and vice versa.

DECA/FBLA-style competitive-simulation participation demonstrates applied business-scenario reasoning and communication skill, but is NOT entrepreneurship evidence in the 'originate and test a real venture' sense -- it is a simulation, not the operation of a real business. Do not conflate the two evidence types.

'Environmental science' and 'sustainability' are not the same activity profile -- a student drawn to fieldwork/conservation and one drawn to sustainability policy/business practice are both legitimately in this family but benefit from different exploration experiences.

Never state a probability of admission/success/outcome without a validated statistical model backing it -- restates the founder spec's non-negotiable #5 as an explainability rule for why[]/warnings[] text specifically.

Never let a ProfileGap (Oryn's own developmental judgment) imply a university 'requires' addressing it -- only a sourced, per-university RequirementEvaluationSummary is allowed to make a requirement-style claim.

Never hide low confidence behind confident-sounding language -- a confidence:'low' recommendation must lead with the data gap itself, not bury it in a trailing warning the student might not read as carefully.

Distinguish 'verified information' from 'Oryn analysis' in the actual RENDERED text a student sees, not just internally in the data model -- externally-sourced content (a requirement's own reasoning) should be visually/textually distinguishable from Oryn's own developmental judgment.

A deprioritize/avoid_for_now recommendation's why[] must always include a redirect -- either the specific higher-value gap it's implicitly weighed against, or an honest statement that it's simply not currently a priority given time constraints -- never a bare 'this is low value' with no comparison point.

Every piece of reasoning this research package contributes must enter why[]/warnings[] as a parameterized template string keyed to a real structured fact -- never as a place where an LLM is asked to 'explain this in your own words' for the deterministic pipeline. Richer nuance that doesn't fit a short template belongs in the optional LLM narration layer's input context, still wrapped in the existing untrusted-data boundary -- never a relaxation of the deterministic pipeline's no-free-text rule.

Never present a specific named opportunity/program sourced only from secondary/aggregator discovery as a confirmed, current, verified offering to a student -- it must first pass through ORYN's actual opportunity-acquisition/verification pipeline. This research package documents pathway TYPES, not a verified directory.

rules.statement: Never infer a student's aptitude, interest, or fit for any field from a demographic attribute (nationality, gender, school type, socioeconomic signal, or any similar proxy).
rules.note: Directly restates the mission brief's own explicit 'what Oryn must not do' list verbatim; minted here because neither branch had numbered it explicitly yet, though both branches' actual document content is already consistent with it throughout.

rules.statement: Never present one career family as objectively 'better' than another (e.g., by salary or prestige) independent of the specific student's own stated interests/goals.

Never equate a career family's aggregate popularity or labor-market growth rate with a claim about a specific student's likely fit or success in it -- every BLS growth statistic cited across this package's family docs is an aggregate US labor-market data point, never a claim about an individual student's prospects.

Where a UK-facing student needs career-outlook grounding, prefer National Careers Service job profiles over BLS/O*NET -- they are the UK's own official equivalent, not a secondary source, and salary/qualification framing does not transfer across countries even when the occupation name is identical.

Turkey's TMMOB chamber-registration/title-protection system is structurally distinct from BOTH the US PE system (voluntary-until-triggered-by-specific-practice) and the UK CEng system (institution-administered chartered status layered on top of an unrestricted base right to practice) -- a Turkey-target engineering student should not have US/UK licensure framing applied to them by default.

Never apply US-holistic-admissions-derived reasoning (depth-over-breadth, extracurricular signaling, redundancy/saturation logic) with the same directness to a student targeting an admissions system with a fundamentally different structure -- e.g. Turkey's exam-score-dominated YKS placement (where academics is doing nearly all the admissions work and the other 8 ProfileDimensions matter for real development but should not be framed as admissions-relevant), or the UK's UCAS system (which weights subject-relevant super-curricular engagement over general extracurricular breadth more heavily than US holistic review does). Oryn's developmental framing remains valid regardless of geography; its ADMISSIONS-RELEVANCE framing must be geography-conditional. Assessed as the single highest-leverage open item this whole research package surfaced (verified independently by both sessions).
rules.note: Originally surfaced by the peer session's persona-testing pass, independently verified by this session via direct ÖSYM/YKS and UCAS sourcing. Highest-priority item for any future continuation of this research.

rules.statement: Unlike DECA/FBLA-style simulated-scenario competitions (RULE-COUNSEL-214), UK's Young Enterprise Company Programme genuinely clears the 'real, tested venture' bar for entrepreneurship evidence -- real company, real bank account, real customers, not a simulation. A UK student's participation should be evaluated against the founder spec's 'idea -> built -> tested' ladder, not treated as equivalent to a DECA/FBLA placement.

Absent a specific target-university signal, a target_geography='turkey' student should be treated as PROBABLY YKS-track by default for the purposes of RULE-COUNSEL-228 (not framing Oryn's developmental dimensions as admissions-relevant) -- not because every Turkey-targeting student is YKS-track (some target private/foundation universities with their own supplementary admissions criteria, or study abroad), but because YKS-track public-university placement is the larger, more common case, and wrongly suppressing US-holistic-style framing for a private/abroad-track student is a much less harmful failure mode than the reverse. Revisit the moment the student adds a specific target university whose actual admission model can be checked.
rules.note: Surfaced by this session's own persona-stress-test of RULE-COUNSEL-228 against a concrete hypothetical (14-year-old, Turkey, no target universities yet) -- found that the rule's own 'targeting Turkish public university placement specifically' condition has no way to be checked for a young student, and needed an explicit default.

rules.statement: The peer branch's 05-redundancy-saturation.md grounds its 'do not recommend more of an already-strong area' logic in two justifications: signal-quality-to-evaluators, and opportunity-cost-under-time-constraint. For a YKS-track student (RULE-COUNSEL-228/230), only the opportunity-cost justification remains valid -- there is no evaluator reading a holistic file in YKS placement, so the signal-quality justification asserts something false if included in an explanation shown to a YKS-track student. Construct avoid_for_now/redundancy explanations for YKS-track students from opportunity-cost alone.
rules.note: Found by checking RULE-COUNSEL-228's Turkey caveat directly against the peer branch's own redundancy-saturation document rather than leaving it as an unspecified general pointer.

rules.statement: 'Wanting to teach' is not one undifferentiated interest -- elementary generalist, secondary subject-specialist, and special education involve substantially different day-to-day work and, in most systems, different credentialing tracks.

Subject-matter achievement is not the same evidence as enjoying/being effective at teaching that subject -- sustained, structured tutoring or instruction of others is meaningfully stronger evidence for the education/teaching family than subject mastery alone.

Turkey's teaching-credential system is actively changing (MEB material indicates a new Milli Egitim Akademisi training requirement beyond KPSS) -- do not give a Turkey-target student a static one-time description of this pathway; re-verify against MEB's current guidance.
rules.note: Sourced from MEB's own regulation for the existing KPSS/pedagogical-formation structure (high confidence); the National Education Academy transition itself is secondary-reported, not yet fetched from MEB's own final rule text (medium confidence for that specific claim).

rules.statement: US, UK, and Turkey teaching credentialing all converge on the same two-part structure (a relevant degree plus a separate pedagogical/professional credentialing step) despite very different specific mechanics -- state this general pattern to students while being explicit the exact mechanics are country-specific and must not be conflated.

For a student with more than one active target geography carrying materially different admissions logic, never silently pick one target's admissions-relevance framing and present it as universally true -- either give a per-target breakdown of why a recommendation matters differently to each, or default to the most-specific/most-active target's framing (never a bare geography-average).
rules.note: Surfaced by the peer session's persona-testing pass (persona H: IB curriculum, mixed UK/Germany targets). An open product/UI design question, not fully resolved by this research -- which of the two options is better is flagged for open-questions tracking on both branches.

rules.statement: 'Music' or 'performing arts' spans meaningfully different day-to-day activities and, sometimes, genuinely different admission mechanisms (e.g. classical conservatory audition vs. general performing-arts degree) -- probe which a student means before treating it as one interest.

Turkish conservatory/performing-arts admission is NOT purely academic-exam-driven the way the general YKS system is (RULE-COUNSEL-228) -- it is a hybrid of a lower TYT score threshold plus a talent/audition exam, structurally closer to the UK's 'talent can substitute for credentials' pattern. Do not apply the blanket YKS caveat to a Turkey-target student interested specifically in this family without this refinement.
rules.note: Verified directly against official Turkish state-conservatory talent-exam guidance, not secondhand.

rules.statement: yearsUntilGraduation <= 0 is not one situation -- distinguish a genuine gap year (Phase 2 framing still applies, often more urgently), actual progression to undergraduate stage (a different product surface entirely, out of this package's scope), and stale profile data (a past-due graduation_year the student never updated) before recommending anything. Never collapse these into one generic 'graduated' treatment.
